title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (helm + terraform)
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: enable fully-automated tenant RBAC bootstrapping for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) via the installer toolchain. Customers installing Redwood Private via the Helm chart + Terraform bundle need a safe, auditable way to provision tenant-scoped roles, initial bootstrap service accounts, and least-privilege cluster-level permissions that the installer can apply without manual intervention. This PR adds automation to the rbac-policy-bundle to support the Private installer workflow and to the Helm/Terraform artifacts to drive idempotent bootstrapping. Changes in this PR: 1) New templated role-sets for tenant isolation (tenant-admin, tenant-viewer, tenant-infra) with parameterized namespace and resource prefixes; 2) A bootstrap permalink that the installer can call (terraform module output + helm hook) to create initial tenant service accounts and bind minimal cluster roles required for next-phase provisioning; 3) Automated generation of least-privilege cluster roles for installer operations (CRD reads, namespace creation, storageclass listing) with explicit deny examples documented; 4) Terraform module updates to emit RBAC manifests and a one-shot "bootstrap" apply target; 5) Helm chart hooks that wait for bootstrap completion and write a status ConfigMap for idempotency; 6) Integration test harness updates (k8s-integration) to cover tenant creation/rollback flows; 7) Added audit policy examples and migration notes for existing Private installations. Checklist: - [x] Spec for role naming and scoping reviewed with security - [x] Terraform and Helm outputs validated in staging cluster - [x] Integration tests added and passing in CI - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-4321, ENG-4365) - [x] Release notes drafted Testing and rollout notes: use the new terraform module target `rbac_bootstrap` in a staging VPC; the Helm chart exposes `rbac.bootstrap.enabled=true` and requires the installer service account token to be provided as a Kubernetes secret. For upgrades: the bootstrap is safe to re-run (idempotent) - it will skip already-created tenants and will attempt no destructive changes. If a tenant rolls back to a prior installer, the new role templates are backward-compatible; operators should follow the migration notes in RELEASE_NOTES. Security: minimal cluster roles were scoped after threat modeling (see ENG-4365). Audit logs are emitted by the installer and workloads are isolated per-tenant. Known limitations: does not yet support cross-tenant shared resources (future work).
